claim: bucketing the drop merge by integer cell removes the O(n^2) pairwise scan while absorbing exactly the same drops
measurement: same fixtures, runner and release build, 3 processes each. entity_heavy: tick 666976us -> 339037us (x1.97), drop stage 478372us -> 149337us (x3.20). entity_heavy_furnaces x1.94 and x3.19. The other six fixtures x0.99-1.00 tick and x0.96-1.00 drop stage. Whole-process CPU 1.7401-1.7457s -> 1.0227-1.0241s.
cause: drop_tick merged same-item nearby drops with a nested loop over every pair, about 180000 pairs per tick at 600 drops
method: bucket drops by integer cell. A pair within 0.5 blocks differs by at most one on each axis, so only the own cell and its 26 neighbours are candidates.
equivalence: iterate i in original order, collect candidates from the 27-cell neighbourhood, filter to j > i, sort ascending, merge on the first match. Drops outside the neighbourhood would fail the distance test anyway, so the first match is unchanged.
rejected: sorting the drops then comparing neighbours changes which drop is absorbed, so it is not equivalent
reordering: the cheap item and distance tests now run before the component-blob Vec comparison. All conditions are conjunctions, so the result is unchanged.
real_bug_fixed: cx + dx overflowed the i32 limit and panicked. floor() saturates on out-of-range coordinates, so a drop at the world edge could trigger this in production. Now checked_add; wrapping was rejected because it aliases cell keys and could merge unrelated drops.
tests: 34 passed, 0 failed, 1 explicitly ignored, serial and at 8 threads
equivalence_test: a verbatim copy of the original pairwise scan is compared against production across 9 scenarios: coincident drops, x and y integer-boundary straddles, mixed items and components, stack cap rejection, age-based survivor selection, far-apart non-merge, chains, and deterministic scatter
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force
remaining: entity_heavy is still 339ms per tick with the drop stage at 149ms. The bucket is O(n x neighbourhood), so 600 drops concentrated in a small area still pay a large neighbourhood. This target is spatially spread load, not a pile.
